title: Spreadsheet references and cycle detection
instructions:
Implement a small integer spreadsheet with references and addition/subtraction.

## Files
- `spreadsheet.py`

`normalize_cell(name) -> str` strips outer whitespace, uppercases, and requires
ASCII letters followed by a positive decimal row number with no leading zero
(e.g. `AA12`). Invalid strings raise `ValueError`. Names are always strings.

`parse_formula(formula) -> list[tuple[int, int | str]]` parses a string beginning
with `=` after outer whitespace is stripped. Operands are unsigned ASCII integers
(leading zeros allowed) or cell references (case-insensitive). Binary operators
are `+` and `-`. One optional unary `+` or `-` is allowed only before the first
operand. Whitespace may separate tokens but cannot split an integer or reference.
Return terms as `(sign, operand)`, sign 1 or -1, integer operands as int, references
normalized to uppercase. Example `=-a1 + 02 - B3` -> `[(-1, 'A1'), (1, 2), (-1, 'B3')]`.
Empty expressions, adjacent operands, trailing operators, further unary operators,
parentheses, and unsupported characters raise `ValueError`.

`Spreadsheet()` starts empty. Implement:
- `set(name, value) -> None`: value is an int (not bool) or a formula string;
  other types raise `TypeError`. Validate names and parse formulas immediately;
  invalid input must not replace an existing cell. Undefined references and cycles
  are allowed at set time. Integers can be negative.
- `get(name) -> int`: recursively evaluate current cell contents. Missing cells
  (including referenced ones) raise `KeyError`; a cycle reached during this
  evaluation raises `ValueError`. Unrelated cycles do not affect a valid cell.
  Updates/deletions must affect subsequent evaluations; shared dependencies are
  not cycles. Do not use Python eval.
- `delete(name) -> None`: remove the normalized name; missing cells raise `KeyError`.
All three methods normalize names using `normalize_cell`.
